andhraPradesh.headline: AP orders protective irrigation and crop-rescue measures as Kharif drought stress affects 2.44 lakh hectares
facts: At a review on 13 September, Agriculture Minister K. Atchannaidu directed officials to use available water for protective irrigation and accelerate field-level crop assessments.
From 1 June to 12 September, Andhra Pradesh recorded 218.2 mm rainfall against a normal 476.1 mm—a 54.2% deficit, according to figures presented at the review.
Kharif crops covered 26.50 lakh hectares by 12 September, about 74% of the normal area.
Moisture stress was reported across 2,44,443 hectares in 284 mandals and 1,792 Rythu Seva Kendras/villages; 10,582 hectares were reported completely dried.
Kurnool had the largest affected area at 1,09,255 hectares, followed by Nandyal at 80,751 hectares and Anantapur at 32,456 hectares.
Officials were asked to promote less water-intensive alternatives; the irrigation minister urged farmers under Nagarjuna Sagar and Srisailam to consider dryland crops.
andhraPradesh.summary: Previous: Andhra Pradesh’s El Niño-linked monsoon deficit and Kharif stress had been covered. Today: the 13 September ministerial review reported 2,44,443 hectares affected, identified the most affected districts and directed protective irrigation, updated crop-health surveys and promotion of less water-intensive crops.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Monsoon variability, drought management, agricultural vulnerability and irrigation policy in Andhra Pradesh.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Know the reported rainfall deficit, affected area, affected mandals and the three districts with the largest crop-stress areas; these are review-date figures, not a final damage assessment.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess how timely crop-health data, protective irrigation, interdepartmental coordination and crop diversification can reduce drought losses and improve climate resilience.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct state-specific link: rainfall, Kharif cultivation and affected-area figures are for Andhra Pradesh, with district-level data for Kurnool, Nandyal and Anantapur.

andhraPradesh.headline: CRDA monitoring data puts Amaravati works at 27.37% physical progress against a 49.71% target
facts: A report citing CRDA project-monitoring data said Amaravati works had reached 27.37% physical progress against a 49.71% target.
The same report put the value of work orders awarded across projects at ₹42,472.80 crore.
It reported physical progress valued at ₹8,514.38 crore and financial progress through running-account bills of ₹6,510.16 crore.
The figures indicate reported progress against scheduled targets; they do not signify project completion.
andhraPradesh.summary: A 13 September report cited CRDA monitoring figures showing that reported physical progress in Amaravati was below the target for the stage. The figures are relevant to capital-region infrastructure execution and should be read as a progress snapshot, not as a completion measure.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Capital-region planning, urban infrastructure, project monitoring and public expenditure.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Distinguish physical progress, financial progress and awarded work value; the reported 27.37% is physical progress, not expenditure or completion.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss transparent milestone tracking, contractor accountability, coordination and realistic scheduling in large capital-city infrastructure programmes.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Amaravati is Andhra Pradesh’s capital-region development project; the reported monitoring figures concern works in the capital region.

sources.title: Amaravati projects lag, reach only 27% physical progress

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh advances statewide smart LED street-lighting programme, with Visakhapatnam work prioritised
facts: Andhra Pradesh plans to replace 10.5 lakh conventional streetlights across urban local bodies with smart LED lights, in collaboration with Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL).
The report said GVMC was taking up identified stretches in Visakhapatnam, with work there expected to finish by the end of September.
The reported first phase envisages 7.5 lakh smart LED streetlights and lighting-management controls across ULBs by March 2027.
Agreements for implementation were reported as completed with more than 120 ULBs; field surveys were under way in several municipalities.
The programme is projected to save 19.57 million units of electricity annually; this is a projection, not an observed saving.
andhraPradesh.summary: Officials reviewed the smart street-lighting programme on 13 September, with Visakhapatnam’s identified stretches prioritised ahead of the CII Partnership Summit scheduled in November. The statewide programme is still being rolled out, and the stated electricity saving is an estimate.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Urban local governance, energy efficiency, smart-city infrastructure and climate mitigation.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: EESL is the implementation partner named in the report; distinguish the 10.5-lakh statewide plan from the 7.5-lakh first phase.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Examine how municipal energy-efficiency projects can reduce electricity costs and emissions, and why performance monitoring and maintenance matter after installation.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The programme covers Andhra Pradesh ULBs, with implementation activity specifically reported in Greater Visakhapatnam.

sources.title: Vizag smart streetlighting project gathers pace ahead of CII Summit

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh proposes a dedicated town-planning cell for high-rise building applications
facts: A 13 September report said the State government had decided to create a dedicated mechanism for high-rise building applications.
The proposed cell is to be established in the Directorate of Town Planning.
It is intended to process applications for buildings with five floors and above and speed up scrutiny and clearances.
The measure was reported as a planned administrative change; the report did not establish that the cell was already operational.
andhraPradesh.summary: The State government was reported to be planning a dedicated town-planning cell to process applications for buildings of five floors and above. The proposal is aimed at streamlining scrutiny and clearances; it should not be treated as an already functioning service.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Urban planning, municipal administration, regulatory simplification and ease of doing business.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The reported proposal concerns buildings with five floors and above and places the proposed cell in the Directorate of Town Planning.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Evaluate how specialised approval mechanisms can reduce procedural delays while retaining safety, environmental and land-use scrutiny.
andhraPradesh.apLink: This is a reported Andhra Pradesh government urban-planning proposal affecting building approvals in the State.

sources.title: AP govt to set up spl cell to clear hurdles to high-rise building plans

andhraPradesh.headline: Rising Sabari inflows prompt Polavaram spillway releases; Dowleswaram discharges water to the sea
facts: As reported for Sunday evening, 13 September, 2,16,956 cusecs were released downstream through the Polavaram spillway amid rising Godavari and Sabari inflows.
The report said the rising water submerged the Gandi Pochamma temple area and access was stopped by temple authorities.
At the Dowleswaram barrage, 110 gates across its four arms were raised and 1,70,849 cusecs were being released to the sea.
The report forecast inflows of about two lakh cusecs by Monday morning; that figure was a forecast, not an observed measurement.
andhraPradesh.summary: Heavy rain in the Sabari catchment was reported to have increased inflows around the Polavaram project. The reported spillway and Dowleswaram releases are operational responses to river flows; the subsequent inflow estimate remained a forecast at the time of reporting.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Godavari basin, multipurpose river projects, flood routing and downstream water management.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Polavaram is on the Godavari system; distinguish the reported Polavaram spillway release from the Dowleswaram discharge to the sea.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss the need to coordinate reservoir operations, flood warnings and local access restrictions across interconnected river infrastructure.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The discharge figures and impacts reported are at Polavaram and Dowleswaram in Andhra Pradesh’s Godavari basin.

sources.title: పెరుగుతున్న గోదారి | Godavari River Rises as Floodwaters Surge at Polavaram

andhraPradesh.headline: APSDMA issues 14 September rain and lightning forecast for districts across Andhra Pradesh
facts: APSDMA warned that a low-pressure system over the northwest Bay of Bengal could bring rain to parts of Andhra Pradesh on 14 September.

The advisory named Parvathipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Polavaram, Kakinada, NTR, Guntur, Palnadu, Markapuram, Nandyal, YSR Kadapa, Annamayya, Chittoor and Tirupati for possible light-to-moderate rain with lightning in places.
Light rain was possible in other districts; the advisory was a forecast, not a report of observed rainfall.
The alert advised people, including farm workers, to avoid exposed areas and shelter under trees or near hoardings during thunderstorms.
andhraPradesh.summary: Previous: A low-pressure-related rain alert for Andhra Pradesh had been covered earlier in September. Today: APSDMA issued a fresh advisory for 14 September, naming districts at risk of rain and lightning and reiterating safety guidance; these were forecast conditions.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Bay of Bengal weather systems, district-level disaster preparedness and lightning safety.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Identify APSDMA as the State disaster-management authority; the listed districts were under a forecast advisory, not a confirmed rainfall report.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Explain how timely, geographically specific warnings and accessible risk communication can reduce lightning-related harm, particularly for farmers and rural communities.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The forecast and safety advice were issued for Andhra Pradesh, with named districts across the State.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh reports 2,876 operating MSME units across 19 inaugurated parks
facts: At a Visakhapatnam event on 13 September, the MSME Minister said 19 MSME parks had been inaugurated and 138 were under construction.
The Minister reported that 2,876 units had commenced operations in the parks.
The State’s stated plan is to establish 175 MSME parks, one in each Assembly constituency.

The report also noted a State agreement with Meta for social-media promotion of MSME products and efforts to help units access online marketplaces; it gave no project-specific investment or jobs figure.
andhraPradesh.summary: At the AP Chamber Expo in Visakhapatnam, the MSME Minister shared the reported status of the State’s MSME-park rollout: 19 parks inaugurated, 138 under construction and 2,876 operating units. The 175-park figure is a plan, not a completed network.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: MSME development, industrial clusters, entrepreneurship and employment-led regional growth.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Separate the reported operational units and inaugurated parks from the State’s target of 175 parks and the 138 parks still under construction.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess whether constituency-level MSME infrastructure, finance access and market linkages can support dispersed entrepreneurship and balanced regional development.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The park counts and operating-unit figure concern Andhra Pradesh; the report specifically records the announcement at a Visakhapatnam expo.

national.headline: IAF inaugurates Dronathon-2026 and demonstrates indigenous Vayu UTtaM system
facts: The Indian Air Force inaugurated Dronathon-2026 at Pokhran Field Firing Range, Jaisalmer, on 14 September.
The three-day event, scheduled for 14–16 September, brought together over 20 defence companies, start-ups, MSMEs, DPSUs and innovators.
Demonstrations cover surveillance, autonomous operations, swarm technologies, electronic warfare and counter-unmanned aircraft systems.
The IAF released its UAS Roadmap to communicate future capability priorities to industry, academia and research organisations.
The IAF demonstrated Vayu UTtaM, an indigenously developed multi-mode unmanned traffic management system, detecting and tracking military and civilian UAS.
national.summary: The IAF launched its first Dronathon to assess unmanned-system technologies under realistic operational conditions. Its opening-day programme included the IAF UAS Roadmap and a Vayu UTtaM demonstration, linking military drone capability with airspace safety and counter-drone needs.
national.staticLink: Indigenisation of defence technology; unmanned aerial systems; airspace management.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Dronathon-2026 was held at Pokhran, Jaisalmer; Vayu UTtaM is an indigenous unmanned traffic management system.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how field trials, industry collaboration and indigenous airspace-management systems can strengthen defence readiness while addressing civilian drone-safety risks.

national.headline: India and MERCOSUR sign protocol recognising electronic Certificates of Origin
facts: India and MERCOSUR signed the First Additional Protocol to their Preferential Trade Agreement on 14 September 2026.
The protocol gives electronically issued Certificates of Origin the same legal validity as paper certificates under Article 16 of Annex III on Rules of Origin.
The India–MERCOSUR PTA was signed on 25 January 2004 and entered into force on 1 June 2009.
The existing PTA provides preferential tariff concessions on 450 tariff lines for India and 452 for the MERCOSUR side.
The protocol will enter into force after each side completes its internal procedures and notifies the other parties.
national.summary: India and MERCOSUR signed an additional protocol to facilitate paperless trade and modernise customs procedures. It recognises electronic Certificates of Origin but is not yet in force; entry into force depends on completion of internal procedures and notification.
national.staticLink: Preferential trade agreements; rules of origin; trade facilitation and digital customs.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The protocol amends Article 16 of Annex III of the India–MERCOSUR PTA and equates electronic Certificates of Origin with paper certificates.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how digital trade documentation can reduce transaction costs, while distinguishing the signing of an agreement from its entry into force.

sources.title: India and MERCOSUR Sign First Additional Protocol to Facilitate Electronic Certificates of Origin
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Commerce & Industry

national.headline: Great Indian Bustard conservation: soft-release centre inaugurated in Kachchh
facts: The Union Environment Minister inaugurated a Great Indian Bustard soft-release centre at Naliya in Kachchh, Gujarat, on 14 September.
The centre is designed to support conservation, monitoring and the gradual adaptation of bustards to the natural environment.
The ministry reported restoration of about 11 sq. km. of grassland affected by invasive Prosopis juliflora and 30 km. of predator-proof fencing covering 15 sq. km.
A chick from the second reported egg-substitution attempt survived beyond its first three months in the wild, according to the ministry briefing.
Thirty-three patrolling and rescue vehicles were flagged off for forest and wildlife conservation work in the Kachchh Forest Circle.
national.summary: Previous: Gujarat’s Great Indian Bustard action plan and conservation measures had been covered. Today: a soft-release centre was inaugurated at Naliya, and officials reported that a chick from the second egg-substitution attempt had survived beyond the critical first three months in the wild.
national.staticLink: Grassland ecosystems; endangered species conservation; in-situ and ex-situ conservation.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The Great Indian Bustard is a grassland bird; the Naliya soft-release centre is in Kachchh, Gujarat.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how habitat restoration, predator-proofing, conservation breeding and community participation can be combined in species-recovery programmes.

sources.title: Union Environment Minister visits Great Indian Bustard Habitat in Kachchh, Gujarat; Inaugurates GIB Soft Release Centre

national.headline: Hindi Diwas and sixth All India Official Language Conference held in Mumbai
facts: Hindi Diwas and the sixth All India Official Language Conference were observed in Mumbai on 14 September 2026; the conference ran for two days.
The Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, organises the annual All India Official Language Conference.
The conference included presentation of the Rajbhasha Gaurav and Rajbhasha Kirti awards for 2025–26 by the Union Home Minister.
The Constituent Assembly adopted Hindi in Devanagari script as the Official Language of the Union on 14 September 1949.
Article 343 concerns the Official Language of the Union; Article 351 directs the Union to promote and develop Hindi.
national.summary: The sixth All India Official Language Conference opened in Mumbai on Hindi Diwas, with the 2025–26 Rajbhasha awards presented as part of the programme. Its constitutional context includes Articles 343 and 351; Hindi is the Union’s Official Language, not the Constitutionally designated national language.
national.staticLink: Official language provisions of the Constitution; linguistic diversity and national integration.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Hindi Diwas marks the Constituent Assembly’s 14 September 1949 decision; relevant provisions include Articles 343 and 351.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss the constitutional framework for the Union’s Official Language alongside India’s multilingual character and the need for inclusive public administration.

sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Home Affairs

national.headline: Social Justice Ministry reports FY 2025–26 SC scholarship disbursements and digital safeguards
facts: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment reported FY 2025–26 releases of ₹562.36 crore under the Pre-Matric Scholarships Scheme for Scheduled Castes and Others, benefiting 26.79 lakh students.
For the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for Scheduled Caste students, it reported ₹6,186.95 crore released in FY 2025–26, benefiting 47.53 lakh students.
From FY 2014–15 to FY 2025–26, reported cumulative central assistance was ₹4,893.03 crore for the pre-matric scheme and ₹46,581.54 crore for the post-matric scheme.
The ministry said the post-matric scheme has used a DBT-enabled framework from FY 2021–22, with transfers to Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts.
Reported safeguards include de-duplication, biometric authentication, e-KYC and digital verification integrations.
national.summary: A ministry update published on 14 September presented scholarship releases and beneficiary figures for FY 2025–26, alongside details of digital delivery and authentication measures. The pre-matric scheme supports school-level continuity, while the post-matric scheme aims to reduce financial barriers to higher education for SC students.
national.staticLink: Centrally Sponsored Schemes; educational inclusion; Direct Benefit Transfer and social-sector accountability.
national.prelimsTakeaway: For FY 2025–26, the ministry reported 26.79 lakh pre-matric and 47.53 lakh post-matric SC scholarship beneficiaries.
national.mainsAngle: Evaluate how DBT and beneficiary verification can improve scholarship delivery, while considering the importance of timely access, grievance redress and inclusion.

sources.title: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment strengthens educational empowerment through scholarships and digital reforms
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

national.headline: Unit II of Bihar’s 1,320 MW Buxar Thermal Power Project enters commercial operation
facts: SJVN reported the commercial operation of Unit II, rated at 660 MW, of the 1,320 MW Buxar Thermal Power Project on 14 September.
The project is located at Chausa in Buxar district, Bihar, and is implemented by SJVN Thermal Private Limited, a wholly owned SJVN subsidiary.
Unit II’s commercial operation is distinct from the overall project capacity: the full project is rated at 1,320 MW.
SJVN said the project is intended to help meet Bihar’s energy requirements.
national.summary: SJVN commemorated the commercial operation of the second 660 MW unit at its Buxar Thermal Power Project. The unit’s operational status is a completed milestone; the project’s total planned capacity is 1,320 MW.
national.staticLink: Energy infrastructure; thermal power generation; public-sector enterprises.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Buxar Thermal Power Project is at Chausa, Bihar; SJVN Thermal Private Limited implements it, and each unit is rated at 660 MW.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss the role of new generation capacity in energy security and the need to balance reliability with environmental and transition objectives.

national.headline: National Patient Safety Conference concludes at AIIMS Nagpur
facts: The National Conference on Patient Safety 2026 concluded at AIIMS Nagpur on 14 September after two days of deliberations.
It was organised by AIIMS Nagpur with the National Patient Safety Secretariat, Directorate General of Health Services and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
The theme was “Safe Care for Non-Communicable Diseases” and the slogan was “Safe Care for Life!”.
Sessions addressed medication and surgical safety, infection prevention, incident reporting, emergency care, technology and patient-family engagement.
The conference provided a national platform for sharing patient-safety practices; recommendations were expected to inform policy and strategy refinement.
national.summary: The conference brought together healthcare leaders and practitioners to discuss safer and more patient-centred care, with particular attention to non-communicable diseases. Its sessions covered clinical safety, incident learning, technology and institutional quality improvement.
national.staticLink: Public health systems; quality of care; patient safety and health-service governance.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The 2026 National Conference on Patient Safety concluded at AIIMS Nagpur under the theme “Safe Care for Non-Communicable Diseases”.
national.mainsAngle: Explain how standardised safety systems, incident reporting, continuous improvement and patient engagement can strengthen public healthcare delivery.

international.headline: Houthi forces capture Greater and Lesser Hanish islands near Bab el-Mandeb
facts: Yemen’s Houthi forces captured Greater Hanish and Lesser Hanish islands in the southern Red Sea, according to reports citing Yemeni officials.
The Hanish islands are about 160 km north of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a strategic maritime passage linking the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.
The advance adds to Houthi control around the Bab el-Mandeb approaches and heightens risks to regional shipping and maritime oil movements.
The island capture was reported amid renewed fighting between Houthi forces and Yemen’s internationally recognised government.
international.summary: Reports on 14 September said Houthi forces had taken Greater and Lesser Hanish, extending their position along a strategically important Red Sea shipping corridor. The development raises concerns over maritime security and disruption risks for trade and energy transport.
international.staticLink: Strategic sea lanes, chokepoints and the geopolitics of the Red Sea and Indian Ocean.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Locate the Bab el-Mandeb Strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa; it connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.
international.mainsAngle: Assess how conflict around maritime chokepoints can affect energy security, international trade and freedom of navigation.

international.headline: G20 Energy Abundance Ministerial opens in Houston with India’s participation
facts: The G20 Energy Abundance Ministerial meetings began in Houston, United States, on 14 September and were scheduled to run through 16 September.
The United States hosted the meetings under its G20 presidency.
India’s Union Minister for Power and Housing & Urban Affairs, Manohar Lal, was participating for India.
The announced discussion pillars included energy security and affordable baseload, permitting and regulatory efficiency, and critical-mineral supply-chain resilience.

A G20 Regulatory Efficiency Symposium was held by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency in Houston on 14 September; it discussed permitting and investment approaches. No ministerial outcomes are recorded here as having been concluded on this date.
international.summary: The Houston ministerial opened on 14 September, bringing energy security, affordability, infrastructure and critical-mineral supply chains onto the G20 agenda. India’s participation provided a forum to present its energy-system priorities; the ministerial was still underway on the date covered.
international.staticLink: G20, global energy governance, energy security and critical-mineral supply chains.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the host city, dates, Indian representative and the ministerial’s three announced discussion pillars.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss how energy security, affordability, clean-energy transitions and resilient critical-mineral supply chains can be balanced in multilateral forums.

international.headline: European Arctic Summit calls for a stronger EU role in the Arctic
facts: The European Arctic Summit was held in Rovaniemi, Finland, on 13–14 September 2026, hosted by Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo.
Leaders from 12 countries—Finland, Denmark, Estonia, France, Greece, Germany, Latvia, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Poland, Romania and Sweden—issued a joint statement on 14 September.
The statement described the Arctic as strategically important for European and global security and called for a more active EU role in the region.
The summit’s agenda included security alongside climate change, critical minerals, energy, infrastructure, logistics, trade routes and sustainable development.
EU High Representative Kaja Kallas said a new EU Arctic Strategy was expected later in 2026; it had not yet been issued at the summit.
international.summary: The Rovaniemi summit concluded with a joint statement urging a stronger European role in the Arctic as the region’s strategic, environmental and economic significance grows. Discussions linked climate change and emerging maritime routes with security, resources and infrastructure.
international.staticLink: Arctic geography, climate change, polar shipping routes and geopolitics.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Rovaniemi is in Finland; the summit statement focused on the Arctic’s strategic importance and called for a stronger EU role.
international.mainsAngle: Examine how Arctic warming is reshaping access to shipping routes and resources, while creating environmental and security challenges.

international.headline: WHO validates Chile for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies as a public-health problem
facts: The World Health Organization validated Chile for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies as a public-health problem on 14 September 2026.
WHO described Chile as the first country in South America to receive this validation.
Chile’s last reported human rabies case transmitted by dogs occurred in 1972; the country maintained vaccination, surveillance, laboratory capacity and access to post-exposure prophylaxis.
WHO validation recognises sustained interruption of dog-mediated transmission and the capacity to prevent its re-emergence; it is not a claim that rabies has been eradicated globally.
WHO identified the achievement as an example of a One Health approach involving human, animal and environmental health.
international.summary: WHO’s validation recognised Chile’s long-term dog-rabies prevention and surveillance programme. The case highlights how vaccination, timely post-exposure care and coordination across human and animal health systems can sustain disease control.
international.staticLink: Zoonotic diseases, public-health surveillance and the One Health approach.
international.prelimsTakeaway: WHO validated Chile as the first South American country to eliminate dog-transmitted rabies as a public-health problem; the last reported human case was in 1972.
international.mainsAngle: Explain how integrated animal vaccination, surveillance and post-exposure prophylaxis support zoonotic disease prevention under One Health.

sources.title: Chile becomes first country in South America validated for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies as a public health problem

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the WHO validation granted to Chile on 14 September 2026?
options: Chile was validated for eliminating all forms of rabies worldwide.
Chile was validated for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies as a public-health problem and was the first South American country to receive this validation.
Chile became the first country globally to eliminate rabies transmitted by all animal species.
WHO validated Chile after its last human rabies case in 2026.
mcqs.explanation: The validation concerns dog-mediated transmission as a public-health problem, not global eradication of rabies. WHO identified Chile as the first country in South America to receive it.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following statements about the Buxar Thermal Power Project is correct?
options: Unit II, rated at 660 MW, entered commercial operation; the overall project is rated at 1,320 MW.
The entire 1,320 MW project entered commercial operation as a single unit.
Unit II is rated at 1,320 MW, while the overall project is rated at 660 MW.
The project is located in Kachchh district, Gujarat.
mcqs.explanation: SJVN reported commercial operation of the 660 MW Unit II at Chausa in Buxar district. The full project capacity is 1,320 MW.

mcqs.question: At the time of the 14 September review, which district had the largest reported area under Kharif moisture stress in Andhra Pradesh?
options: Nandyal
Anantapur
Kurnool
Kakinada
mcqs.explanation: Kurnool had 1,09,255 hectares affected, followed by Nandyal with 80,751 hectares and Anantapur with 32,456 hectares.

mcqs.question: Which of the following was reported as a feature of the IAF's Dronathon-2026?
options: It was a completed international air exercise held in Houston.
It included demonstrations of surveillance, autonomous operations, swarm technologies, electronic warfare, and counter-UAS systems.
It was organised to validate Chile's rabies-control programme.
It focused exclusively on civilian street-lighting systems.
mcqs.explanation: Dronathon-2026 was inaugurated at Pokhran Field Firing Range and included demonstrations across those unmanned-system capability areas.

74% against a 54.2% target

mcqs.question: Which statement about Andhra Pradesh's smart LED street-lighting programme is correct?
options: The programme's projected annual electricity saving was reported as an already observed saving.
The plan covers 10.5 lakh conventional streetlights, while its first phase envisages 7.5 lakh smart LED streetlights by March 2027.
The programme is limited to Visakhapatnam and has no other urban local bodies involved.
The report stated that all 10.5 lakh lights had already been replaced.
mcqs.explanation: The state plan covers 10.5 lakh lights, with 7.5 lakh envisaged in the reported first phase. The projected 19.57 million units of annual savings is not an observed result.
